messages:
kevin: Heads up — our dedicated pool in us-west-2 for tiered-dedicated-1 is full and we're spilling into hosted. Seeing increased latencies and ~8% 5xx on generation paths. ops-bot alerted at 1740325588 :warning:
ops-bot: Alert: GPU utilization for dedicated-pool-us-west-2 >= 98% for 6m. Auto-fallback enabled -> shifting traffic to hosted-us-west-2. Incident ID INC-2026-2147
marta: Copy. How much traffic was shifted? any customers impacted besides internal canaries?
kevin: Rough snapshot: 30% of requests got routed to hosted in the last 5m. Canary apps started returning 500 for some longer contexts (~>1k tokens). P95 latency on hosted jumped from 220ms -> 480ms for generation. Dedicated queue length stayed high (~120 requests queued).
sam: My read: provisioner didn't clear failed nodes; some GPUs are showing ECC errors and one rack lost connectivity to the shard. We're throttling new job placements. I'm pinging infra ops to confirm if hardware or a patch caused evictions.
jin: Oncall checked nodes: 3 nodes in rack r-17 in us-west-2 have repeated NVLINK flaps. Kernel logs show repeated io errors. I isolated the rack, shifted scheduling weights off it. That reduced placement failures but pool capacity still below threshold.
olivia: Can we increase fallback percentage to 50% temporarily while we triage? Need to protect tail-latency for customers. Also flagging cost — hosted is ~2.6x per-token vs dedicated.
sam: We can, but that will blow cost for the day. Proposal: shift non-SLA / low-priority routes first, leave enterprise customers on dedicated unless they hit errors. Update routing policy via `rdrctl`:
```
# shift low-priority routes off dedicated
rdrctl route update --region us-west-2 --pool dedicated-usw2 --offload-tags "free-tier,staging" --pct 100
# increase hosted fallback for remaining traffic to 50%
rdrctl route update --region us-west-2 --pool dedicated-usw2 --fallback-to hosted-usw2 --pct 50
```
kevin: Doing the first command now. Patch applied at 1740325889. Will monitor.
marta: Also open a ticket for on-prem provisioning to replace the two bad nodes and run a rolling replacement. Sam, can you schedule replacement window?
sam: Yep, booked maintenance with hardware team — ETA 4h to get new blades in and run burn-in. I'll start a canary drain+repopulate plan.
jin: Added a temporary spike-protection rule to limit single-customer concurrency to 150 -> 50 on dedicated in us-west-2 to stop noisy neighbors from consuming queue.
kevin: After shifting low-priority routes, queue length dropped to ~45 and 5xx fell to 2.1%. P95 on hosted still elevated but stable at ~420ms.
olivia: We should also enable prefix/KV cache priming for hosted fallback to lower cost + latency for repeated contexts. Can someone toggle cache warmup for the hosted pools?
sam: On it — enabling cache warmup + increasing batch size cap to 64 for hosted fallback. Will monitor throughput impact.
ops-bot: Deploy started: cache-warmup job triggered on hosted-usw2 at 1740326002.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout: routing policy updated, 4 canaries routed to hosted at 1740326020.
marta: Good. Action items: (1) Sam replace nodes (owner: sam), (2) Keep low-priority offload until pool healthy (owner: kevin), (3) Monitor cost delta and report (owner: olivia), (4) Put postmortem on calendar after stabilization (owner: marta).
kevin: Agreed. If anything spikes we'll escalate to capacity-oncall. For now I'll keep a heartbeat every 10m. :thumbsup:
